provenance.environment: Docker Desktop on shared Windows authoring host; sequential worker; deterministic local provider; concurrent host activity was not isolated
provenance.method: Pinned Locust 20 users/spawn 5/run-time 30s, wait 0.05-0.15s; reset PostgreSQL and Redis and restart worker before each run. Observation window starts before Locust process launch and ends after process exit, so includes process startup/shutdown and differs from Locust internal Requests/s denominator. SQL counts accepted_at <= cutoff and COMPLETED updated_at <= cutoff; worker stopped after cutoff. Jaeger coldline.process_exception and model_provider.summarize spans entirely within the same window. Span counts agree with SQL completions in this capture. No Redis XLEN backlog measurement is asserted.
reproduction_commands: SELECT state, accepted_at, updated_at FROM exceptions;
provenance.capture_limit: Small shared-host sample, no controlled CPU profile, no measured production provider or cloud bottleneck. Rates are window averages, not maximum sustainable capacities.

worker_service_capture.precision: Pooled service duration rounded to six decimals is the supplied calculation input.

historical_two_user_capture.limitations: Original capture has no preserved common-cutoff unfinished-job counts or pure worker-service observations. XLEN is stream length, not backlog. Accepted-to-terminal sum/count includes queue wait even at light load. Capture host and timestamps were not retained. Do not use these data to size workers.

operating_policy.formula: required_workers = ceil(arrival_jobs_per_second * service_seconds_per_job * (1 + 0.30)); apply margin once and ceiling once at the end. This planning model assumes sequential homogeneous workers and ignores scaling contention until measured.

two-worker-pilot.trigger: Projected offered load divided by one-worker modeled service capacity exceeds one.
two-worker-pilot.rollback: Any duplicate side effect or database p95 above 200 ms.
two-worker-pilot.measure: Completion rate, oldest outstanding age, database p95 and duplicates with two workers.

admission-control-pilot.trigger: Observed arrival exceeds one-worker modeled service capacity.
admission-control-pilot.rollback: Rejected requests exceed 1% or oldest outstanding age exceeds 60 seconds.
admission-control-pilot.measure: Admission rejections, oldest outstanding age and completion rate.

operating_policy.scope: Recommend exactly one reversible local pilot. Compare both other named alternatives. No production deployment or multi-region platform migration is supported. Thresholds are hypothetical policy inputs, not observed metrics.

claims.C01: The historical 0.29 seconds is pure worker service time.
claims.C02: Historical XLEN values 44 and 45 prove unfinished-job backlog.
claims.C03: 1.53 API requests/second is completed-worker throughput and maximum capacity.
claims.C04: At the supplied 10x sensor rate, 500 bytes x 1000 readings/second gives 1800000000 MB/hour.
claims.C05: At 1000 readings/second and an exception fraction of 0.012, arrival is 120 jobs/second.
claims.C06: Seven days of raw readings require 43.2 GB total storage.
claims.C07: Required workers = ceil(ceil(arrival x service) x 1.3 x 1.3).
claims.C08: API p95 + worker p95 always equals end-to-end p95.
claims.C09: These local runs justify immediate multi-region Kubernetes, a service mesh and a managed multi-region stream.
claims.C10: The 10x arrival rate is an authored planning assumption, not a measured 10x run.

fidelity.worker_topology: one sequential worker in supplied capture
fidelity.percentile_rule: Marginal p95 values alone do not determine the joint end-to-end p95; use correlated end-to-end observations.
